d.title: 1139 - cloudflare: Cloudflare Reverse Proxies are Dumping Uninitialized Memory - project-zero
Advanced Flash Vulnerabilities in Youtube
d.summary: Part one maps YouTube's Flash player architecture, security sandboxes, wrappers, and dynamically loaded modules. It shows how permissive domain trust and access to child objects can expose user information, while drawing parallels to client-side HTML5 component boundaries.
d.context: Another installment in the same research series.

d.title: Advanced Flash Vulnerabilities in Youtube
d.summary: Part two abuses YouTube's appLoader behavior to load an attacker-controlled SWF into the youtube.com security domain. The resulting cross-site Flash condition permits attacker code to inherit trusted origin privileges and make cross-domain requests.
d.context: Another installment in the same research series.

d.title: Advanced Flash Vulnerabilities in Youtube
d.summary: Part three races and reloads YouTube's Flash wrapper so the main application derives a module URL from an attacker-controlled loader URL. The injected module then combines the trusted sandbox with permissive cross-domain policy to read otherwise protected data.
d.context: Another installment in the same research series.

d.title: Advanced Flash vulnerabilities in Youtube
d.summary: Part four forces YouTube's iframe API into its Flash fallback and analyzes the JavaScript-to-Flash messaging bridge. It develops three cross-site scripting paths in the youtube.com embed context by combining the fallback player with crafted messages and Flash behavior.
d.context: Another installment in the same research series.

d.title: Gone In Six Characters: Short URLs Considered Harmful for Cloud Services
d.summary: The authors show that short URL token spaces can be brute-forced at scale, exposing OneDrive files and Google Maps directions. Predictable OneDrive identifiers let a single discovered link reveal other shared content, while writable folders enable malware injection that synchronizes to users' devices; sampled Maps links also disclosed sensitive travel patterns.
d.context: The authors' summary explains the same study for a broader audience and links the full paper as its technical source.

d.title: Host-of-Troubles Vulnerabilities, leading to HTTP cache poisoning and Firewall bypass
d.summary: The project documents inconsistent parsing of ambiguous Host headers across servers, proxies, CDNs, and firewalls. Crafted requests produce cache poisoning and policy bypasses, including transparent Squid caches, Akamai-backed paths, WAFs, and parental controls; it recommends rejecting multiple Host headers and whitespace before field names.
d.context: The project page accompanies the paper and provides the authors' overview of the host-header ambiguity research.
